text: Let $S_{n}$ be the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic progression. If $S_{3n} = 3S_{2n}$, then the value of $\frac{S_{4n}}{S_{2n}}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let a be first term and d be common diff. of this A.P.

Given, $S_{3n} = 3S_{2n}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{3n}{2}[2a+(3n-1)d]=3\frac{2n}{2}[2a+(2n-1)d]$

$\Rightarrow 2a+(3n-1)d=4a+(4n-2)d$

$\Rightarrow 2a+(n-1)d=0$

Now, $\frac{S_{4n}}{S_{2n}}=\frac{\frac{4n}{2}[2a+(4n-1)d]}{\frac{2n}{2}[2a+(2n-1)d]}=\frac{2\left [2a+(n-1)d_{=0}+3nd\right ]}{\left [2a+(n-1)d_{=0}+nd\right ]}$

$=\frac{6nd}{nd}=6$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text: The locus of the centroid of the triangle formed by any point P on the hyperbola $16x^{2}-9y^{2}+32x+36y-164=0$, and its foci is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given hyperbola is 

$16(x+1)^{2}-9(y-2)^{2}=164+16-36=144$

$\Rightarrow \frac{(x+1)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{16}=1$

Eccentricity, $e=\sqrt{1+\frac{16}{9}}=\frac{5}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ foci are (4, 2) and ($-$6, 2)


[IMG]

Let the centroid be (h, k) & A($α$, $β$) be point on hyperbola.

So, $h=\frac{α-6+4}{3},k=\frac{β+2+2}{3}$

$\Rightarrow α=3h+2,β=3k-4$

($α$, $β$) lies on hyperbola so

$16(3h+2+1)^{2}-9(3k-4-2)^{2}=144$

$\Rightarrow 144(h+1)^{2}-81(k-2)^{2}=144$

$\Rightarrow 16(h^{2}+2h+1)-9(k^{2}-4k+4)=16$

$\Rightarrow 16x^{2}-9y^{2}+32x+36y-36=0$

text: The value of the definite integral $\int\limits _{π/24}^{5π/24}\frac{dx}{1+\sqrt{3\tan 2x}}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $I=\int\limits _{π/24}^{5π/24}\frac{(\cos 2x)^{1/3}}{(\cos 2x)^{1/3}+(\sin 2x)^{1/3}}dx$ ...... (i)

$\Rightarrow I=\int\limits _{π/24}^{5π/24}\frac{\left (\cos \left \{2\left (\frac{π}{4}-x\right )\right \}\right )^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}{\left (\cos \left \{2\left (\frac{π}{4}-x\right )\right \}\right )^{\dfrac{1}{3}}+\left (\sin \left \{2\left (\frac{π}{4}-x\right )\right \}\right )^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}dx\left \{\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(a+b-x)dx\right \}$

Hence, $2I=\int\limits _{π/24}^{5π/24}dx$ [(i) + (ii)]

$\Rightarrow 2I=\frac{4π}{24}\Rightarrow I=\frac{π}{12}$

text: If b is very small as compared to the value of a, so that the cube and other higher powers of $\frac{b}{a}$ can be neglected in the identity $\frac{1}{a-b}+\frac{1}{a-2b}+\frac{1}{a-3b}+.....+\frac{1}{a-nb}=αn+βn^{2}+γn^{3}$, then the value of $γ$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(a-b)^{-1}+(a-2b)^{-1}+....+(a-nb)^{-1}$

$=\frac{1}{a}\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}\left (1-\frac{rb}{a}\right )^{-1}$

$=\frac{1}{a}\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}\left \{\left (1+\frac{rb}{a}+\frac{r^{2}b^{2}}{a^{2}}\right )+(termstobeneglected)\right \}$

$=\frac{1}{a}\left [n+\frac{n(n+1)}{2}.\frac{b}{a}+\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}.\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}\right ]$

$=\frac{1}{a}\left [n^{3}\left (\frac{b^{2}}{3a^{2}}\right )+.....\right ]$

So, $γ=\frac{b^{2}}{3a^{3}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=1+xe^{y-x},-\sqrt{2}<x<\sqrt{2},y(0)=0$

then, the minimum value of $y(x),x\in \left (-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy-dx}{e^{y-x}}=xdx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy-dx}{e^{y-x}}=xdx$

$\Rightarrow -e^{x-y}=\frac{x^{2}}{2}+c$

At x = 0, y = 0 $\Rightarrow$ c = $-$1

$\Rightarrow e^{x-y}=\frac{2-x^{2}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow y=x-\ln \left (\frac{2-x^{2}}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=1+\frac{2x}{2-x^{2}}=\frac{2+2x-x^{2}}{2-x^{2}}$


[IMG]

So minimum value occurs at $x=1-\sqrt{3}$

$y\left (1-\sqrt{3}\right )=\left (1-\sqrt{3}\right )-\ln \left (\frac{2-\left (4-2\sqrt{3}\right )}{2}\right )$

$=\left (1-\sqrt{3}\right )-\ln \left (\sqrt{3}-1\right )$

text:
Let g : N $\to$ N be defined as

g(3n + 1) = 3n + 2,

g(3n + 2) = 3n + 3,

g(3n + 3) = 3n + 1, for all n $\geq$ 0. 

Then which of the following statements is true?
options: There exists an onto function f : N $\to$ N such that fog = f
There exists a one-one function f : N $\to$ N such that fog = f
There exists a function f : N $\to$ N such that gof = f
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g$ maps each block $\{3n+1,3n+2,3n+3\}$ onto itself as the cycle $3n+1\to 3n+2\to 3n+3\to 3n+1$, so $g(x)$ always lies in the same block as $x$ and $g(x)\neq x$.

Option (C): three applications of the cycle return every element, so $g\circ g\circ g(x)=x\neq g(x)$; (C) is false.

Option (B): if $f$ is one-one, $f(g(x))=f(x)$ forces $g(x)=x$, which never holds; (B) is false.

Option (D): $g(f(x))=f(x)$ requires $f(x)$ to be a fixed point of $g$, and $g$ has none; (D) is false.

Option (A): take $f(3n+1)=f(3n+2)=f(3n+3)=n+1$ for $n\geq 0$. Since $x$ and $g(x)$ are in the same block, $f(g(x))=f(x)$ for every $x$, and $f$ takes every value $1,2,3,\ldots$, so $f$ is onto; (A) is true.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text:
Let $f:[0,\infty )\to [0,\infty )$ be defined as $f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}[y]dy$

where [x] is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Which of the following is true?
options: f is continuous at every point in $[0,\infty )$ and differentiable except at the integer points.
f is both continuous and differentiable except at the integer points in $[0,\infty )$.
f is continuous everywhere except at the integer points in $[0,\infty )$.
f is differentiable at every point in $[0,\infty )$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f:[0,\infty )\to [0,\infty ),f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}[y]dy$

Let $x=n+f,f\in (0,1)$

So, $f(x)=0+1+2+...+(n-1)+\int\limits _{n}^{n+f}ndy$

$f(x)=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+nf$

$=\frac{[x]([x]-1)}{2}+[x]\{x\}$

Note $\lim _{x\to n^{+}}f(x)=\frac{n(n-1)}{2},\lim _{x\to n^{-}}f(x)=\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2}+(n-1)$

$=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$

$f(x)=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}(n\in N_{0})$

so f(x) is cont. $\forall$ x $\geq$ 0 nd diff. except at integer points

text: Let y = y(x) be solution of the following differential equation $e^{y}\frac{dy}{dx}-2e^{y}\sin x+\sin x\cos ^{2}x=0,y\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=0$ If $y(0)=\log _{e}(α+βe^{-2})$, then $4(α+β)$ is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $e^{y} = t$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dt}{dx}-(2\sin x)t=-\sin x\cos ^{2}x$

$I.F.=e^{2\cos x}$

$\Rightarrow t.e^{2\cos x}=\int e^{2\cos x}.(-\sin x\cos ^{2}x)dx$

$\Rightarrow e^{y}.e^{2\cos x}=\int e^{2z}.z^{2}dz,z=e^{2\cos x}$

$\Rightarrow e^{y}.e^{2\cos x}=\frac{1}{2}.\cos ^{2}x.e^{2\cos x}-\frac{1}{2}\cos x.e^{2\cos x}+\frac{e^{2\cos x}}{4}+C$

at $x=\frac{π}{2},y=0\Rightarrow C=\frac{3}{4}$

$\Rightarrow e^{y}=\frac{1}{2}\cos ^{2}x-\frac{1}{2}\cos x+\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{4}.e^{-2\cos x}$

$\Rightarrow y=\log \left [\frac{\cos ^{2}x}{2}-\frac{\cos x}{2}+\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{4}e^{-2\cos x}\right ]$

Put x = 0

$\Rightarrow y=\log \left [\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{4}e^{-2}\right ]\Rightarrow α=\frac{1}{4},β=\frac{3}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text: Let $\vec{p}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{q}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ be two vectors. If a vector $\vec{r}=(α\hat{i}+β\hat{j}+γ\widehat{k})$ is perpendicular to each of the vectors ($(\vec{p}+\vec{q})$ and $(\vec{p}-\vec{q})$, and $\left |\vec{r}\right |=\sqrt{3}$, then $|α|+|β|+|γ|$ is equal to $_______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{p}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ (Given )

$\vec{q}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$

Now, $(\vec{p}+\vec{q})\times (\vec{p}-\vec{q})=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 3 & 5 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right |$

$=-2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-2\widehat{k}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}=\pm \sqrt{3}\frac{\left ((\vec{p}+\vec{q})\times (\vec{p}-\vec{q})\right )}{\left |(\vec{p}+\vec{q})\times (\vec{p}-\vec{q})\right |}=\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}\left (-2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-2\widehat{k}\right )}{\sqrt{2^{2}+2^{2}+2^{2}}}$

$\vec{r}=\pm \left (-\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\widehat{k}\right )$

According to question 

$\vec{r}=α\hat{i}+β\hat{j}+γ\widehat{k}$

So, |$α$| = 1, |$β$| = 1, |$γ$| = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $|α|+|β|+|γ|$ = 3
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text:
The term independent of 'x' in the expansion of 
$\left (\frac{x+1}{x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1}-\frac{x-1}{x-x^{1/2}}\right )^{10}$, where x $\neq$ 0, 1 is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (\frac{x+1}{x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1}-\frac{x-1}{x-x^{1/2}}\right )^{10}$

= $\left (\frac{\left (x^{1/3}\right )^{3}+\left (1^{1/3}\right )^{3}}{x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1}-\frac{\left (\sqrt{x}\right )^{2}-(1)^{2}}{x-x^{1/2}}\right )^{10}$

= $\left (\frac{\left (x^{1/3}+1\right )\left (x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1\right )}{x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1}-\frac{\left (\sqrt{x}+1\right )\left (\sqrt{x}-1\right )}{\sqrt{x}\left (\sqrt{x}-1\right )}\right )^{10}$

= $\left (\left (x^{1/3}+1\right )-\frac{\left (\sqrt{x}+1\right )}{\sqrt{x}}\right )^{10}$

= $\left (\left (x^{1/3}+1\right )-\left (1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right )\right )^{10}$

= $\left (x^{1/3}-\frac{1}{x^{1/2}}\right )^{10}$

[Note:

For $\left (x^{α}\pm \frac{1}{x^{β}}\right )^{n}$ the $(r+1)^{th}$ term with power m of x is 

$r=\frac{nα-m}{α+β}$]

Here $α=\frac{1}{3}$, $β=\frac{1}{2}$ and m = 0

then $r=\frac{10\times \frac{1}{3}-0}{\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{2}}$ = $\frac{10}{3}\times \frac{6}{5}$ = 4

$\therefore$ $T_{5}$ is the term independent of x.

$\therefore$ $T_{5} =$ ${}^{10}C_{4}$ = 210
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text: Let $S=\left \{n\in N\left |\left (\begin{array}{ll} 0 & i \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right )^{n}\left (\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right )=\left (\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right )\forall a,b,c,d\in R\right \} \right.$, where i = $\sqrt{-1}$. Then the number of 2-digit numbers in the set S is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $X=\left (\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right )$ & $A=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 0 & i \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right )^{n}$

$\Rightarrow$ AX = IX
